section_summary: This section traces American and British efforts to obtain written assurances for their oil companies under Japan’s Petroleum Industry Law. It records disputes over sales quotas and tariffs, the Japanese Foreign Office’s January 1937 confirmation of earlier assurances, and continuing concern about reduced quotas in Korea. A separate despatch surveys Japan’s plans to produce liquid fuel from coal and alcohol.

subfiles.title: Incoming cablegram concerning Japanese oil quotas and tariff proposals
subfiles.about: Parker relays reports of discriminatory quotas, proposed tariffs, and requests for diplomatic intervention.
subfiles.summary: The continued cable reports kerosene allocations favoring Japanese refiners, proposed petroleum tariffs and a gasoline tax, and plans for a fuel alcohol monopoly. Parker urges an immediate approach to the State Department about the companies’ uncertain trading position.

subfiles.title: Transmittal to the American Ambassador in Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a December 17 conversation memorandum concerning Japan’s oil situation.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the conversation memorandum and its attachments for the Ambassador’s information.

subfiles.title: Transmittal to the American Ambassador in London
subfiles.about: Forwards the December 17 conversation memorandum and enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Sends the memorandum about a Standard-Vacuum representative’s discussion with Department officers.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram No. 264 on proposed oil representations
subfiles.about: Discusses the form and timing of American and British representations to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Clive’s concern that routine approaches will accomplish little and considers representations to Japanese ambassadors in Washington and London. He favors emphasizing the companies’ uncertainty, while avoiding demands or an approach that would embarrass the Foreign Minister.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram No. 265 requesting urgent preliminary action
subfiles.about: Reports oil companies’ request for a diplomatic approach before holiday quota and tariff decisions.
subfiles.summary: The companies fear penalties over unfulfilled storage duties and discriminatory tariff changes. Grew awaits authorization and a parallel British step.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram No. 266 on British instructions
subfiles.about: Seeks urgent instructions after Clive receives authority for representations.
subfiles.summary: Grew favors simultaneous, substantially identical approaches by the two embassies.

subfiles.title: Department telegram No. 164 authorizing representations
subfiles.about: Authorizes an approach to Japan while prescribing a measured tone.
subfiles.summary: The Department approves coordinated representations in Tokyo and a later informal discussion with the Prime Minister if appropriate. It declines, for now, approaches to Japanese ambassadors in Washington and London.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram No. 268 reporting December 24 interview
subfiles.about: Reports presentation of an aide memoire to Japan’s Foreign Minister.
subfiles.summary: The Minister received Grew cordially and promised to study the matter; the British Ambassador made a similar approach.

subfiles.title: Parker letter quoting Yokohama cable
subfiles.about: Relays a company cable about the December 24 diplomatic approaches.
subfiles.summary: Parker quotes a report of the ambassadors’ requests for fair treatment and written assurances.

subfiles.title: Incoming Yokohama cable quoted by Parker
subfiles.about: Reports American and British approaches to Japan’s Foreign Minister.
subfiles.summary: A faint copy of the cable quoted in Parker’s letter.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck reply to Parker
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Parker’s account of the December 24 approaches.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck confirms receipt of a similar Embassy report and offers to share useful information.

subfiles.title: Division note on Japan’s liquid fuel plans
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokyo despatch No. 2183 on coal liquefaction and fuel alcohol.
subfiles.summary: Notes the proposed state backed coal liquefaction company, doubts about production targets, and plans for an alcohol monopoly and gasoline blending.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Search for Oil
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese plans to develop domestic liquid fuel substitutes.
subfiles.summary: The despatch describes coal hydrogenation plants planned or under construction in Japan and Manchuria, a proposed holding company to finance liquefaction, and an alcohol monopoly with compulsory gasoline blending. It outlines a national fuel policy of subsidies, research, tariffs, and taxes. The Embassy doubts the near term production targets but expects some eventual reduction in dependence on imported fuel.

subfiles.title: No action note
subfiles.about: Records that no action on a telegram appears necessary.
subfiles.summary: States that no action is called for.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram No. 3 on Korean sales quotas
subfiles.about: Reports substantial reductions in foreign companies’ first half 1937 Korean oil quotas.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports a 37.7 percent gasoline quota cut and plans informal American and British inquiries at the Foreign Office.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram No. 4 on Foreign Office reaction
subfiles.about: Reports Dickover’s and Sansom’s conversations with Matsushima.
subfiles.summary: Matsushima appeared sympathetic and said Arita was pressing for a prompt settlement of the foreign oil companies’ position.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 2194
subfiles.about: Recommends forwarding Grew’s despatch and later telegram to London.
subfiles.summary: Notes that subsequent written assurances have overtaken much of the despatch’s account.

subfiles.title: American Oil Interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Recounts negotiations for written assurances and the December 24 diplomatic representations.
subfiles.summary: Grew details the companies’ failed attempt to obtain clear written confirmation of oral assurances, citing unfavorable kerosene allocations, proposed tariffs, and a sharply worded Mining Bureau reply. He explains American and British discussions about the appropriate diplomatic response. Both ambassadors then made separate, substantially similar representations to the Japanese Foreign Minister on December 24; the despatch supplies five enclosures.

subfiles.title: Joint company request for four assurances
subfiles.from: Rising Sun Petroleum Company and Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.to: Ogawa Gotaro, Minister of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Requests written assurances on quotas, prices, equal treatment, and stockholding compensation.
subfiles.summary: The companies report a Mitsui storage arrangement, apologize for delay, and seek confirmation of four trading assurances.

subfiles.title: Joint company request concerning Chosen and Taiwan
subfiles.from: Rising Sun Petroleum Company and Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.to: Ogawa Gotaro, Minister of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Seeks similar trading assurances for Chosen and Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Requests the Ministry’s good offices for assurances in both territories.

subfiles.title: Mining Bureau reply to Standard-Vacuum
subfiles.to: C. E. Moyer, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Orders prompt fulfillment of oil stockholding duties and addresses the four requested assurances.
subfiles.summary: Demands a storage timetable and says the requested points will receive consideration.

subfiles.title: American Embassy aide memoire
subfiles.about: Requests a clear statement of intentions toward American oil interests.
subfiles.summary: Seeks confirmation that Japan will permit continued, reasonably secure and profitable American oil operations.

subfiles.title: British Embassy note verbale
subfiles.about: Requests written assurances for Rising Sun Petroleum’s future trade in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The note recounts prolonged negotiations, oral assurances, the unsatisfactory Ministry reply, and new concerns over quotas and tariffs. It asks Japan to clarify its intentions and provide assurances that would allow British oil interests to continue operating.

subfiles.title: Division note on telegram No. 6
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s written confirmation of earlier oral assurances.
subfiles.summary: Expresses hope for settlement and states that no action is required.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram No. 6 conveying Japanese reply
subfiles.about: Transmits Japan’s note verbale confirming four oil company assurances.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office denies any intent to discriminate against or expel American oil interests and says its earlier reply confirmed the four points. An unofficial paper defends the kerosene allocation and tariff proposal. The American and British embassies welcome the written confirmation.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of telephone conversation with Parker
subfiles.about: Records Parker’s discussion with Dooman about British action and the Foreign Office’s reaction.
subfiles.summary: Parker reports Eden’s conversation with Japan’s ambassador in London. Dooman relays encouraging indications from Tokyo, and Parker hopes continued efforts will secure assurances.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Tokyo despatch and related records to London
subfiles.about: Forwards despatch No. 2194, a conversation memorandum, and telegram No. 6.
subfiles.summary: Sends copies of records covering the negotiations and Japan’s reply.

subfiles.title: Copy of Tokyo telegram No. 6
subfiles.about: Copies Japan’s confirmation of assurances and explanations on quotas and tariffs.
subfiles.summary: A reproduced, partly paraphrased version of the January 15 telegram enclosed with the London transmittal.

subfiles.title: Division note concerning Parker’s telephone inquiry
subfiles.about: Records Parker’s reaction to learning of Tokyo’s January 15 telegram.
subfiles.summary: Parker understood the Department’s assumption that his Japan representatives would report the development.

subfiles.title: Parker request for the Japanese reply
subfiles.about: Requests the substance of the Japanese Foreign Minister’s reply.
subfiles.summary: Parker says Yokohama reported that the Embassy had telegraphed the reply.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck reply to Parker
subfiles.about: Shares the Japanese reply and confidential explanation of quotas and tariffs.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck encloses the note verbale, relays the unofficial Japanese explanations, and expresses hope for settlement.

subfiles.title: Translation of Japanese note verbale enclosed for Parker
subfiles.about: Confirms the four assurances and denies an intent to exclude American oil interests.
subfiles.summary: A copy of the formal Japanese reply, conditioned on the company fulfilling its legal obligations.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 2233
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Korean quota dispute and the written assurances discussed in Grew’s despatch.
subfiles.summary: Distinguishes Korean quotas from the assurances for Japan Proper and notes the attached Japanese replies.

subfiles.title: American Oil Interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reviews Korean quota reductions, Japan’s written assurances, and the companies’ prospects.
subfiles.summary: Grew details sharp reductions in foreign companies’ Korean quotas while a Korean refiner receives increased allocations. He recounts informal approaches to Matsushima and the January 15 Japanese notes confirming assurances for Japan Proper, though the explanations of kerosene quotas and tariffs remain troubling. Company representatives foresee limited growth in Japan Proper and Taiwan, possible further losses in Korea, and substantial storage costs. The despatch continues beyond page 393.
